notes.meaning: The Lord spoke to Moses to give formal penalties for laws previously announced. Earlier chapters warned the conscience against sin, but now civil punishments were established. Those who were not restrained by the fear of God would be held back by the fear of judgment.

Any Israelite or resident foreigner who sacrificed a child to the false god Molech was condemned to die. The entire community was responsible to stone the offender. This public execution showed that child sacrifice was a horrible crime against God and the whole nation.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest that giving seed to Molech might have referred to dedicating children into pagan cultic service or rituals rather than killing them by fire.

notes.meaning: God warned that He would directly oppose anyone who offered a child to an idol. Such a horrific sin defiled God's sacred dwelling place among them and dragged His holy name through shame. Even if human judges failed to see the crime, God Himself would cut off the wrongdoer.

If the community turned a blind eye and refused to execute a person who sacrificed a child to Molech, God Himself promised to step in. He would bring judgment on that person, their family, and everyone who joined in such unfaithfulness. Tolerating terrible evil makes an entire community share in the guilt.

Anyone who sought advice or help from mediums and fortune-tellers was committing spiritual unfaithfulness against God. Turning away from the Lord to consult demonic spirits brings divine anger. God promised to intervene directly and cut off anyone who engaged in the occult.

God called His people to separate themselves from evil customs and live holy lives. They were to obey His statutes faithfully because the Lord Himself was the one making them holy. Following God's good rules is how believers reflect His clean and loving character.

Anyone who cursed their father or mother faced the death penalty. This did not mean an accidental harsh word, but an adult's bitter contempt and settled hostility toward their parents. Rebellious disrespect tore down God-given family authority and brought severe guilt upon the offender.

If a man committed adultery with a neighbor's wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress were to be put to death. Adultery broke the sacred marriage covenant and deeply wounded the family. God's law treated the destruction of marriage as a grave capital crime.

A man who had sexual relations with his father's wife committed both incest and adultery. This shameful act brought dishonor on his father and shattered natural family decency. Because both people knowingly took part in this wicked act, both were condemned to die.

A man who had sexual relations with his daughter-in-law committed a perverse disruption of family life. It twisted the natural order God designed, confusing the roles of child and grandchild. Both individuals were held guilty and punished with death.

Sexual relations between two men were defined as an abomination, going directly against God's design for human sexuality. Consenting partners in this act were subject to capital punishment under Israel's civil law. God required His covenant people to maintain complete moral and sexual purity.

Marrying both a woman and her mother was condemned as extreme depravity. The law ordered those who entered into this relationship to be burned with fire to rid the camp of such wickedness. God demanded the complete removal of practices that degraded family honor.

Any man or woman who engaged in sexual acts with an animal was to be put to death. The animal was also killed to wipe away every reminder of the unnatural deed and prevent further corruption. God created clear boundaries between humans and animals that must never be crossed.

Sexual relations between a brother and sister, whether full or half siblings, was a disgraceful crime. Such incestuous unions brought shame upon the household and breached family trust. Both the man and woman were cut off from among their people for this offense.

Intentionally having sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period resulted in both partners being cut off. Menstrual blood made a person ritually unclean, which meant they could not approach God's sanctuary for worship. Disregarding these boundaries showed a careless disrespect for God's holiness.

Sexual relations with an aunt on either the father's or mother's side were strictly forbidden. Close blood relations were barred from marriage or intimacy to protect the dignity of the family. Anyone who broke this rule bore the weight of their own sin.

A man who slept with his uncle's wife showed deep disrespect to his uncle and committed an incestuous act. The civil courts were not ordered to execute them, but God reserved the penalty for Himself. They would bear their guilt and remain childless as a divine judgment.

Taking a brother's wife was an unclean act that dishonored the brother's marriage. The only exception was the special command to care for a brother's childless widow, which did not apply here. Those who entered this forbidden marriage faced God's judgment of dying childless.

God urged Israel to obey all His commandments so that the Promised Land would not vomit them out. The Canaanites had filled the land with these abominable practices, which is why God detested their ways and drove them out. Israel was commanded never to imitate the corrupt lifestyle of pagan cultures.

The Lord promised to give Israel a rich and fertile land filled with abundance. He had personally chosen them and separated them from all the other peoples of the earth. Because of this special calling, they were expected to live faithfully for Him.

Israel was commanded to distinguish carefully between clean animals fit for food and unclean ones that were forbidden. Daily meal choices served as an ongoing reminder of their special covenant with God. Following these dietary rules kept Israel distinct from the corrupt practices of surrounding nations.

The Lord reminded Israel that they were to be holy because He is holy. He set them apart from every other nation so that they would belong entirely to Him as His treasured people. True worship calls for hearts and lives that reflect God's moral purity.

Any man or woman who worked as a medium or spiritist was to be put to death by stoning. Practicing the occult was direct rebellion against God and opened the community to spiritual ruin. The practitioners brought the sentence of death entirely upon themselves.
